claims.author: tankyleo
claims.harm: dumping sensitive transaction data to disk on broadcaster-only nodes expands the attack surface and privacy risk
claims.quote: I have reservations about dumping sensitive data to disk on node shutdown. Previously a non-wallet, broadcaster-only node would not persist any sensitive data to disk, but with this PR it now does.

claims.author: vasild
claims.harm: unrestricted permissions on privatebroadcast.dat could leak sensitive private broadcast data
claims.quote: Make sure the file gets permissions `0600`.

claims.author: craigraw
claims.harm: a shutdown-dump approach does not solve transaction eviction from mempools or crashes, unlike a proper persistent broadcast pool
claims.quote: However, I don't think this change goes far enough (or at least, should be considered a first step). Losing broadcasted transactions due to a node restart is probably quite rare.

notes: Initial record for draft PR #34322. Tankyleo raised privacy/security concerns about writing broadcast records to disk on non-wallet nodes; Vasild provided Concept ACK with a reminder about 0600 permissions; Craigraw supported the concept but suggested a broader broadcast pool architecture, which the author agreed with as a better long-term design.

participants.note: raised concerns about persisting sensitive broadcast tx data to disk on broadcaster-only nodes
Concept ACK; notes benefits outweigh disk concerns, suggested 0600 file permissions and retention option
Concept ACK; suggested the approach doesn't go far enough and should consider a persistent broadcast pool

support.author: vasild
support.reason: benefits of not losing transactions across restarts outweigh concerns about storing on disk

support.author: craigraw
support.reason: agrees with persisting broadcast transactions, though suggests a broader broadcast pool approach
